INSERT INTO `paper` (`title`, `year`, `method`, `publish`, `category`, `code_id`, `abstract`, `evaluation`)
VALUES
(
'Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation',
2025,
'CoRAG – Multi-step iterative retrieval with rejection sampling and test-time scaling',
'NeurIPS 2025',
'Dynamic RAG / Multi-hop Reasoning',
20,
'This paper introduces CoRAG (Chain-of-Retrieval Augmented Generation), an approach for training o1-like RAG models that retrieve and reason over relevant information step by step before generating the final answer. Unlike conventional RAG methods that perform a single retrieval step, CoRAG allows the model to dynamically reformulate the query based on evolving state. It utilizes rejection sampling to automatically generate intermediate retrieval chains, augmenting existing RAG datasets. At test time, various decoding strategies scale the model\'s test-time compute.',
'On multi-hop QA benchmarks, CoRAG achieves more than 10 points improvement in EM score over strong baselines. On the KILT benchmark, it establishes new state-of-the-art performance across diverse knowledge-intensive tasks. Comprehensive analyses validate the scaling behavior of test-time compute.'
),
(
'TS-RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Time Series Foundation Models are Stronger Zero-Shot Forecaster',
2025,
'TS-RAG – Retrieval-augmented time series forecasting with Adaptive Retrieval Mixer (ARM)',
'NeurIPS 2025',
'RAG for Time Series / Cross-domain Adaptation',
18,
'TS-RAG is a retrieval-augmented generation framework for time series forecasting that enhances the generalization and interpretability of Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs). It leverages pre-trained time series encoders to retrieve semantically relevant segments from a knowledge base, and uses an Adaptive Retrieval Mixer (ARM) to dynamically fuse retrieved patterns with the model\'s internal representation, improving accuracy without task-specific fine-tuning.',
'On seven public benchmark datasets, TS-RAG achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot forecasting performance, outperforming existing TSFMs by up to 6.84% across diverse domains while also providing desirable interpretability.'
),
(
'Parametric Retrieval Augmented Generation',
2025,
'Parametric RAG – Document parameterization and parameter-level knowledge injection into FFNs',
'SIGIR 2025 (Tutorial + Paper Track)',
'Parametric RAG / Knowledge Injection',
21,
'This paper introduces Parametric RAG, a new RAG paradigm that integrates external knowledge directly into the feed-forward networks of an LLM through document parameterization. Instead of treating retrieved documents as static context prepended to the input, Parametric RAG transforms them into model parameters, achieving deeper and more efficient knowledge integration. This is part of a broader tutorial covering both Dynamic RAG and Parametric RAG directions.',
'Parametric RAG demonstrates improved efficiency and effectiveness compared to traditional in-context RAG methods. DyPRAG (a variant with a dynamic parameter translator) shows scalability and efficiency without maintaining a large corpus of parametric modules.'
),
(
'Overview of the TREC 2025 Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) Track',
2026,
'TREC RAG Track – Standardized RAG evaluation with multi-sentence narrative queries, 4 subtasks',
'TREC 2025 / arXiv 2026',
'RAG Benchmarking & Evaluation',
19,
'This paper presents the overview of the TREC 2025 Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) Track, the second edition building on the 2024 track. It pushes research into systems that integrate retrieval and generation for complex, real-world information needs. The track uses long, multi-sentence narrative queries to better reflect deep search tasks, and employs multi-layered evaluation covering relevance assessment, response completeness, attribution verification, and agreement analysis.',
'The track attracted numerous participants exploring diverse approaches including multi-stage retrieval, nugget-based query decomposition, hierarchical citation processes, and agentic iterative retrieval. The standardized evaluation framework enables systematic comparison of different RAG pipeline designs.'
),
(
'A Systematic Review of Key Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Systems: Progress, Gaps, and Future Directions',
2025,
'Systematic review – Taxonomy of 100+ RAG systems from Naive RAG to multi-modal RAG',
'arXiv 2025',
'Survey & Taxonomy',
NULL,
'This paper presents a comprehensive systematic review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), tracing its evolution from early systems to current state-of-the-art approaches. It examines key RAG systems including Naive RAG, Advanced RAG, Modular RAG, GraphRAG, Self-RAG, HyDE, Corrective RAG, and multi-modal RAG variants. The review identifies critical gaps in RAG research such as hallucination, retrieval quality, scalability, and domain adaptation challenges.',
'The survey covers over 100 RAG systems with detailed taxonomies. It has received 80+ citations in a short period, indicating high impact. It provides structured analysis of progress and gaps, offering future research directions for the community.'
